description: Create an issue in a project visible to this token. Returns the new issue key. Requires permission to create issues in that project. Answers with 'notified' (who this actually reaches) and 'unresolvedMentions' (what looked like a mention and reached nobody, each with a reason) — a wrong handle is stored as written and never refused, so that list is the only sign it did not land.

assignee.description: Assignee username or email. Omit to leave unassigned.

description.description: Issue description. Markdown is kept as written, and carries $…$ / $$…$$ LaTeX formulas and [~username] mentions (the username, which list_users hands you ready-made — never the display name).

dueDate.description: The day this is due, as YYYY-MM-DD. A calendar day, not a timestamp — do not send a time or a zone.

fixVersions.description: The versions of the project this goes out in, by name, comma-separated: '2.4.0' or '2.4.0, 2.4.1' — the names list_versions gives. A name the project does not have refuses the filing and lists the ones it has.

labels.description: Labels to set, space or comma separated.

order.description: Its place among its parent's children: 1, 2, 3… — the order they are to be done in. Children with a place come first, in it; the rest after, by number. Filing a template's sub-tasks, pass 1, 2, 3… in turn.

parentKey.description: Parent issue key, to create this as a child/sub-task.

teamRole.description: The project's team role this issue is for, by name, e.g. 'Звуковик' — one of the roles its administrators keep. With no assignee given, the issue goes to the person who has held that role longest.

type.description: Issue type name, e.g. 'Task', 'Bug', 'Story', 'Epic'. Defaults to 'Task'.

name: create_issue
